promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 6 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: You crushed the plan but overshot it by a lot, so next week pulls volume back, keeps the long run moderate, and starts marathon-pace work on Wednesday.

flags.title: Plan overrun
flags.detail: ran 53 mi vs 43 planned, long run 20 mi vs 15, and added a threshold rep. Felt good is not the same as being ready.

flags.title: Load spike
flags.detail: weekly distance jumped 43 percent from 37 to 53 mi, with relative effort at 423 vs a 3-week average of 223.

flags.title: Long-run intensity
flags.detail: 88 percent of the 20 miler sat in zone 3 with HR drifting 145 to 153, firmer than an easy long run should be.

flags.title: Easy share low
flags.detail: zones 1 and 2 landed at 54 percent against an 80 percent target, partly because the long run was not easy.

flags.title: Calves tight Sunday night
flags.detail: first body-check niggle since the knee in mid August, worth watching this week.

answers.question: I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?
answers.answer:
Short answer: no, not on top of a jump that size. Going from 37 to 53 miles in one week, with a 20-miler that ran in zone 3 for most of it, is exactly the setup that produced the knee flare three weeks ago. Feeling fine right now is the body banking the stress, not absorbing it, and the tight calves on Sunday are the first hint of that bill arriving.

The plan is already working: your easy pace at 9:50 and HR 139 is a big improvement on 10:28 at 151 three weeks ago, and the long run has climbed from 10 to 20 mi. We do not need to force more on top. With 6 weeks to the race, the gains now come from holding the pattern, adding marathon-pace work, and arriving healthy. So this week we cut volume a touch, keep one quality session, and run the long one truly easy.

new.analysis:
## Why the pullback
A 43 percent jump in a single week, with the long run drifting into zone 3 and calves tight afterwards, is a load I want to let settle before we push again. The plan was built to top out around 45 mi this week with a 15 mi long run; you have already banked more than that, so this week acts as the cutback I would otherwise have slotted in next. You are not losing fitness by backing off here, you are letting it stick.

## What changes
I am keeping Wednesday as the one quality day and swapping the threshold reps for marathon-pace work, because at 6 weeks out we want to rehearse the goal effort. Target pace for sub 3:45 is around 8:35/mi, and we start with 5 mi of it in the middle of an 8-mile run. The long run drops to 16 mi and should stay under HR 150 the whole way; if the group pulls it faster, run with them for company only and peel off if the HR climbs.

## How to run the week
Treat Monday and Friday as full rest, not optional easy miles. On the easy days keep the HR under 145 and let pace fall where it wants. If the calves are still talking by Tuesday, add a few minutes of walking before and after, and tell me in the next check-in.

safetyCallouts.title: Watch the calves.
safetyCallouts.body: If tightness turns into sharp pain, pain that worsens run to run, or anything that changes your stride, stop the session and see a physio before the next run. Do not try to run through it.
